name: Weekly_GDP_level_tracker
what_it_holds: Small MIT-licensed repo that visualizes the Eurozone GDP-level index derived from the OECD Weekly Tracker (year-on-year series), i.e. a downstream reprocessing/plotting script rather than a primary data store.
why_useful: Secondary/derivative use of the same OECD Weekly Tracker restricted to Eurozone GDP level — useful as a worked example of how to turn the tracker's YoY series into a level index, but adds no new data beyond the primary repo above.
duplicate_of_holding: Same underlying data as NicolasWoloszko/OECD-Weekly-Tracker, narrower scope
themes: Real-time and weekly economic indicators: OECD Weekly Tracker (Google Trends based), NY Fed WEI, ONS faster indicators, Dallas Fed mobility, Bundesbank weekly activity index
why_all: Secondary/derivative use of the same OECD Weekly Tracker restricted to Eurozone GDP level — useful as a worked example of how to turn the tracker's YoY series into a level index, but adds no new data beyond the primary repo above.

name: bundesbank (R package, CRAN-mirrored as cran/bundesbank)
what_it_holds: R scripts for downloading Bundesbank time-series data via their SDMX-style download interface; long-standing CRAN package, no data files committed, functions to build query URLs and parse the resulting CSV/TSV downloads.
why_useful: Alternative, older/simpler API client for the same Bundesbank series as bbk above (including potentially the weekly activity index); useful as a fallback if bbk's API mapping doesn't cover the desired series.
duplicate_of_holding: Same purpose as m-muecke/bbk, older and simpler
themes: Real-time and weekly economic indicators: OECD Weekly Tracker (Google Trends based), NY Fed WEI, ONS faster indicators, Dallas Fed mobility, Bundesbank weekly activity index
why_all: Alternative, older/simpler API client for the same Bundesbank series as bbk above (including potentially the weekly activity index); useful as a fallback if bbk's API mapping doesn't cover the desired series.

name: mcp-bundesbank-de
what_it_holds: An MCP (model-context-protocol) server wrapping the Deutsche Bundesbank statistics API, brand new (created/updated 13 Sep 2026). No stored data, just a live-query tool interface.
why_useful: Another live-access route to Bundesbank series (including the weekly activity index) for an agent workflow, but functionally redundant with the R clients above and requires running an MCP server.
duplicate_of_holding: Same data source as bbk/bundesbank R packages
themes: Real-time and weekly economic indicators: OECD Weekly Tracker (Google Trends based), NY Fed WEI, ONS faster indicators, Dallas Fed mobility, Bundesbank weekly activity index
why_all: Another live-access route to Bundesbank series (including the weekly activity index) for an agent workflow, but functionally redundant with the R clients above and requires running an MCP server.

name: DallasFedMobility
what_it_holds: Small, old (last updated 2020) repo apparently built around the Dallas Fed's mobility/social-distancing index from the COVID period; no stars, no description beyond the name — could not confirm committed data files vs. a scraping script without cloning.
why_useful: Could point to a source client for the Dallas Fed Mobility and Social Distancing Index, a high-frequency (near-daily) US regional mobility series that could proxy domestic US travel intent; but the index itself may have been discontinued post-2021 and this repo is stale.
geography: US (regional, Dallas Fed district and beyond)
themes: Real-time and weekly economic indicators: OECD Weekly Tracker (Google Trends based), NY Fed WEI, ONS faster indicators, Dallas Fed mobility, Bundesbank weekly activity index

name: nagaatwork/laborlens
what_it_holds: BLS API -> Snowflake -> dbt -> Streamlit pipeline for US labor market data, all 50 states + DC, unemployment rate, SARIMA 6-month-ahead forecasts, monthly refresh via GitHub Actions. Confirmed via README: state-level only (not metro despite description ambiguity), no data files committed to repo (pulled live via BLS API + requires a Snowflake account to run).
why_useful: A working reference pipeline for BLS unemployment-by-state if the team wants a state-level (not metro) unemployment panel as a regional consumer-strength proxy for the NA segment split; but it is state-level, requires Snowflake, and holds no committed data, so it's a method template rather than a data source.
geography: US, all 50 states + DC (state-level, not metro)
size_hint: n/a (no committed data; needs external Snowflake account to run)
themes: FRED / BEA / BLS / Census API clients and curated macro panels (consumer sentiment, PCE services, CPI lodging, airfares, unemployment by metro)
why_all: A working reference pipeline for BLS unemployment-by-state if the team wants a state-level (not metro) unemployment panel as a regional consumer-strength proxy for the NA segment split; but it is state-level, requires Snowflake, and holds no committed data, so it's a method template rather than a data source.
